jobs.title: Audit Operations Lead
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the Role You will run the external audit calendar for our SOX 404 program as we scale toward an IPO. That means coordinating with our external auditors across the year, aligning testing windows with control owners, educating our control owners, and keeping requests and deliverables on schedule. You will also own SOX scoping and risk assessment cycles, deficiency tracking, and status reporting, and help roll out our GRC platform so the program runs from one system of record instead of spreadsheets. You will scale the program through AI-enabled workflows that reduce manual effort and speed up our SOX program. This role reports to the Head of Business Controls and works closely with everyone on the SOX and Internal Audit team. This is an individual contributor role for someone who keeps a complex program on schedule, writes clearly, and makes the program simpler each cycle. Key responsibilities Own the annual SOX audit calendar, including interim and year-end testing windows, walkthrough schedules, and key deliverable dates agreed with external auditors. Serve as the day-to-day point of contact for external auditor requests. Triage, route, and track each request to closure, including PBC (provided-by-client) lists and evidence deliveries. Coordinate auditor walkthroughs and fieldwork with process owners, control owners, and the SOX Testing team, so each control owner is asked for the same evidence once. Track auditor findings, management responses, and deficiency follow-ups, and report status to Internal Audit leadership. Prepare control owners and process owners for auditor sessions, and get evidence delivered on time without direct authority over them. Lead the annual SOX scoping and risk assessment, including quarterly refreshes, and support the annual Fraud Risk Assessment, so the program has appropriate scope and coverage under COSO. Monitor BP and IT SOX testing and report status to leadership and share status with external auditors Lead work with the business to improve control documentation, including education of templates and SOX guidance. Find optimization and automation opportunities across the SOX lifecycle through the use of AI. Support the rollout of the GRC tool for SOX, including control libraries, workflows, evidence requests, and testing templates. Define the data and reporting requirements the platform must meet, and test that it produces what the program needs. Run the quarterly sub-certification process and report results to leadership Own SOX program status reporting: dashboards and metrics for leadership, audit calendar progress, and deficiency and remediation status. Own status reporting for the full SOX lifecycle: scoping and risk assessment, testing, deficiencies and remediation, segregation of duties (SOD), SOC 1 report reviews, the fraud risk assessment, and audit calendar progress. Minimum qualifications Big 4 audit firm experience on SOX 404 or ICFR engagements, including managing audit calendars, PBC requests, and fieldwork with external audit teams. Experience working directly with external auditor teams on requests, testing schedules, and findings, from the company side. Several years of hands-on SOX 404 experience, including scoping, risk assessment, control documentation, testing, and deficiency evaluation. Working knowledge of the COSO framework, ICFR, and PCAOB standards. Experience developing or maintaining Risk and Control Matrices and process documentation or flowcharts. Experience implementing or administering a GRC systems Experience reporting program status, metrics, and issues to senior leadership. Ability to get control owners to deliver on time without authority over them. Clear writing and calm coordination under deadline pressure. A Bachelor's degree in a related field or equivalent experience. Preferred qualifications In-house SOX experience at a pre-IPO or newly public company. Experience running a fraud risk assessment. CPA, CISA, or similar certification. Comfort with SQL or data tools for reporting, and experience building lightweight automations, including with Claude. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $230,000 — $300,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate, QC Analytical, Cell Therapy opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Manager, Global Entity Management
jobs.description: About the role Datadog employs roughly 8,100 people across 35 countries through global subsidiaries, all under a Nevada parent. Some are operating companies. Others came to us through acquisitions. We open in new markets often enough that the structure is always moving, and we manage it in Diligent Entities. This role owns it. The work is entity formation and maintenance in many jurisdictions, corporate records and statutory filings, and daily coordination with the Finance, Tax and People teams. You will deal directly with government agencies, registries, registered agents and local counsel around the world. You will also be the person the rest of the company asks whenever a question touches our corporate structure. The role sits in Legal Operations, and you will report to our Senior Director, Legal Operations, who has supported entity management operations in the past. Our Associate General Counsel, Corporate & Securities owns the work product and sets the standards for entity management and for our securities filings. Legal Operations runs the function; Corporate & Securities owns the substance. The placement also gives you breadth. Legal Operations covers legal technology and systems, process design, outside counsel and spend operations, restricted party and sanctions screening, product legal support, and the department's AI work. We expect to cross-train you across those areas over time, and to cross-train colleagues into entity work. Entity management will remain the substantial majority of this job. On AI in particular, Legal Operations is where most of that work happens for the legal department. We look at how our current tools could be used better, we assess new ones, and we look for ways to extend AI into systems that were never built with it in mind. If you look at a manual process and wonder whether software should be doing it, there is room here for that. On the securities side of the role You will also handle Section 16 filings (Forms 3, 4 and 5), Forms 144 and Rule 10b5-1 plan administration, supervised by our Associate General Counsel, Corporate & Securities, who trains the team on it. Prior public company reporting experience is welcome but not required. We have trained people into this work before and it went well. What we need is someone who wants to learn it and who will hold the deadlines once trained. What you will do Global entity management: the core of the role Entity lifecycle. Manage formations, foreign qualifications, branch registrations, conversions, mergers, dissolutions, liquidations and deregistrations for our US and international entities, working with outside service providers and local counsel in each jurisdiction. Good standing. Keep every entity in good standing wherever it operates. That covers annual reports and returns, statutory filings and business licenses. It also covers records for registered agents and agents for service of process, and the local compliance requirements that differ by country. Government agencies and registries. Deal directly with company registries, tax authorities, chambers of commerce and other government bodies on filings, registrations, certificates and inquiries, some of which need regular follow-up. Compliance calendar. Own the global entity compliance calendar. Know what is due, where and when, and flag it early rather than relying on a service provider's reminder. Directors, officers and authority. Track director and officer appointments and resignations, maintain signature and delegation of authority records, and prepare powers of attorney, incumbency certificates and secretary's certificates. Review the legacy and dormant entities we hold, including those that came in through acquisitions. Form a view on which should be maintained, consolidated or wound down, then carry out the plan. Corporate records and governance Corporate records. Maintain minute books, statutory registers, organizational charts and entity records worldwide, in physical and electronic form, so the portfolio stays audit-ready. Governance documents. Draft board and stockholder resolutions, written consents, minutes for subsidiary matters, and organizational documents such as articles, bylaws and operating agreements, in support of routine governance matters and corporate transactions, for attorney review. Document requests. Turn around internal and external requests for certificates of good standing, certified copies, apostilles and legalizations. These usually block something, so speed matters. jobs.title: Electrical Engineer, PCBA Test Infrastructure, Robotics
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and pushing towards AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world settings. Working across the entire model stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the constraints of physical systems to improve peoples’ lives. ABOUT THE ROLE We are seeking an Electrical Engineer for a senior individual-contributor role leading printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) test infrastructure for advanced robotic systems. You will independently turn evolving requirements into working test stations, make technical tradeoffs, and own delivery from architecture and circuit design through validation, deployment, and reliable operation. This role combines development-lab work with deployment at contract manufacturers. You will develop electrical test systems for board bring-up, programming, functional test, and characterization, partnering with mechanical, firmware, software, manufacturing, and reliability teams to carry validated stations from prototypes into repeat builds. This role is based in San Francisco, CA, and requires in-person presence 4 days a week. Travel to contract-manufacturer sites is part of the role, with timing based on build and deployment needs. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Own PCBA test-station architecture, including device-under-test interfaces, programmable power, electronic loads, signal routing, instrumentation, and protection. - Translate board requirements and likely failure modes into test coverage, measurement methods, and pass/fail criteria. Partner with board designers on design for test, test-point access, programming interfaces, and diagnostics. - Design and bring up fixture interface boards, switching circuits, harnesses, and connectors. Release schematics, PCB layouts, wiring diagrams, bills of materials, and interface definitions. - Integrate oscilloscopes, meters, power supplies, loads, and data acquisition hardware; validate calibration, timing, accuracy, and repeatability across stations and board revisions. - Develop and debug programming and communications interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, and Ethernet as required by the board. Diagnose power, signal-integrity, grounding, and contact problems. - Design and validate current limiting, power sequencing, ESD protection, interlocks, and fault recovery appropriate to the hardware under test. - Partner with mechanical engineers on probe access, connector mating, board support, cooling, and serviceability. Work with firmware and software partners to define interfaces and integrate test stations with shared software. - Write, debug, and maintain test code for instrument control, board programming, automated sequences, diagnostics, and result logging. Collaborate with software partners on reusable frameworks, code reviews, and reliable releases. - Establish station commissioning, calibration, maintenance, and configuration control. Track board identity and revision, firmware version, test limits, and station configuration with each result. - Use reference boards, independent measurements, and deliberate fault checks to distinguish board failures from fixture or software errors. Improve test coverage, false-failure rate, cycle time, and station uptime. - Own test-station deployment and acceptance at contract manufacturers, including station correlation, build support, operator training, and troubleshooting. Release configurations and documentation that keep lab and factory results consistent. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have strong intuition for analog and digital circuits, power delivery, electronics debugging, and reliable measurement. - Move comfortably from architecture and circuit design to soldering, probing, scripting, and troubleshooting in the lab. - Care about grounding, shielding, contact quality, calibration, and evidence that a test detects the faults it is intended to find. - Take ownership from prototype through reliable daily operation, balancing rapid iteration with clear documentation and maintainable test systems. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS - Demonstrated ability to independently deliver significant electronics test-system projects from ambiguous requirements through working hardware, validation, and sustained use. - Hands-on capability in circuit and fixture-interface design, schematic interpretation, board bring-up, power delivery, signal switching, and instrument integration. - Ability to independently debug PCBAs and test hardware using oscilloscopes, meters, logic analyzers, and systematic root-cause investigation. - Ability to write, debug, and maintain code that interfaces with real hardware in Python or a comparable language, including instrument control, sequencing, error handling, and structured result logging. - Practical understanding of grounding, signal integrity, calibration, measurement uncertainty, ESD controls, power sequencing, and electrical protection. - Ability to release clear test and hardware documentation, coordinate across engineering disciplines, and support hands-on deployment and troubleshooting at contract manufacturers. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS - Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. - Prior PCBA functional-test or automated-test-equipment experience, including design for test, test coverage, fixture correlation, and new-product builds at contract manufacturers. - Experience with embedded programming, diagnostic firmware, and board interfaces such as JTAG/SWD, UART, SPI, I²C, CAN, or Ethernet. - Experience with PCB design tools, shared test-automation frameworks, production data systems, or robotics hardware. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE - Commission a reusable PCBA test station with documented coverage, acceptance criteria, and traceable results; deploy and validate a reproducible configuration at a contract manufacturer. - Demonstrate measurement repeatability and intended fault detection using reference boards, independent measurements, and known-fault cases. jobs.title: Software Engineer, Identity Infrastructure
jobs.description: About the Team The Identity Infrastructure Engineering team builds the identity and access systems that OpenAI’s researchers, engineers, and internal teams rely on to protect critical systems and data. We partner with Research, Applied Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, and Security to make secure access practical across cloud and internal environments. About the Role We’re looking for a hands-on software engineer to design and build high-scale, high-throughput secure access proxies and the distributed systems behind them. These are tier-zero services: researchers, engineers, and agents depend on them to reach critical infrastructure safely and reliably. You’ll work at the intersection of networking, distributed systems, and infrastructure security, building the serving paths and control-plane integrations that connect identities to resources. Teleport is a core part of the current platform; the role also includes credential brokers, policy enforcement, and developer-facing integrations. You’ll own the services you build from design and implementation through production. That means understanding human, agent, and workload traffic, improving throughput and tail latency, making authorization decisions auditable, and designing for safe multi-region rollout and recovery. We’re looking for someone who can turn a demanding security requirement into software that works well at scale and is straightforward for other engineers to use. In this role, you will: - Design and implement secure access proxies, gateways, and credential brokers that provide narrowly scoped, auditable access to infrastructure and internal services while reducing standing privileges.. - Integrate identity and access policy across clients, proxies, and target systems so approved permissions take effect promptly and access expires or is revoked when required. Ensure correct behavior when policy is stale or sessions remain active. - Build observability that explains the end-to-end access path: latency, errors, saturation, authorization decisions, and identity attribution, without leaking credentials. - Engineer safe multi-region rollouts, canaries, rollback, failover, and recovery. Validate changes with realistic test environments, load tests, and failure testing. - Keep core access services reliable, performant, and maintainable. Own production support, maintenance, upgrades, and incident recovery; ship durable fixes that reduce recurring failures, alert noise, and manual work. - Make secure access easy to adopt through reusable APIs, client tooling, diagnostics, and self-service workflows. Lead migrations that preserve critical workflows, with tested rollback and recovery paths and clear ownership across Infrastructure, Security, and SRE. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have built and operated production backend, proxy, networking, or infrastructure services with demanding scale or availability requirements. - Have practical networking depth and can reason about HTTP, TCP, TLS, DNS, routing, and load balancing across real request paths. - Can explain how you handled performance bottlenecks, partial failures, multi-region deployment, or a difficult production change in a system you personally built. - Understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, trust boundaries, credential handling, and the consequences of an access-control failure. - Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with Go, Rust, Python, or similar languages. - Use tests, profiling, telemetry, and reproducible experiments to debug across system boundaries and verify correctness, performance, and recovery. - Make practical scope decisions, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and follow through from code to production. Teleport or comparable access-platform experience is helpful; strong engineering and production ownership matter more than knowing every tool. You will design and maintain customer education across Dropbox Learn, product-launch education, learning paths, multimedia tutorials, and other self-service learning experiences. Working closely with cross-functional partners, you will translate complex product capabilities and customer needs into clear, actionable instruction. You’ll combine instructional design principles, digital content production, and responsible AI-assisted workflows to develop scalable learning experiences. Your work will contribute to helping customers become more confident and successful with Dropbox products while improving the consistency, quality, and accessibility of customer education. Responsibilities Design, develop, publish, and maintain engaging, accessible, and accurate customer learning experiences across Dropbox products and education platforms. Create and update web-based training, learning paths, product-launch education, tutorials, multimedia content, and other instructional resources. Translate complex product workflows and customer needs into clear, task-oriented instruction with logical sequencing and actionable next steps. Author, publish, and maintain learning content using Contentful and related content-management and learning-delivery platforms, including quality assurance and localization preparation. Collaborate with Product, Product Marketing, Customer Advocacy, Support, subject-matter experts, and program managers to deliver education aligned with customer and business needs. Responsibly leverage AI tools to support content drafting, storyboarding, synthesis, analysis, and production efficiency while validating outputs for accuracy, accessibility, instructional quality, and customer relevance. Support continuous improvement of learning experiences through reusable templates, documented processes, customer feedback, performance insights, and content-quality standards. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer - Engineer, Chassis & Vehicle Dynamic
jobs.description: About the Team DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. The team's mission is to create technologies that support and augment human networks, aiming to improve efficiency for Dashers, merchants, and consumers alike. We’re ruthlessly focused on business impact. We are a highly senior team composed of former pioneers from a variety of different robotics industries. As of 2025, DoorDash has completed 10B lifetime deliveries. We’re focused on how to do the next 10B even better About the Role We’re looking for a Mechanical Engineer to develop and improve chassis systems and vehicle dynamics performance for DOT, DoorDash’s autonomous delivery robot. You’ll combine hands-on mechanical design, engineering analysis, and vehicle testing to improve existing platforms and develop suspension and chassis solutions for future projects. You’ll own engineering work from requirements and concept development through detailed CAD design, prototype evaluation, and validation. Working closely with internal teams and suppliers, you’ll assess designs, resolve technical challenges, and ensure chassis systems meet our performance, durability, and integration requirements. This role offers the opportunity to influence how DOT rides, handles, brakes, and traverses real-world terrain while improving the reliability and serviceability of our deployed robots. You’re excited about this opportunity because you will… Design and improve suspension and chassis systems , including suspension geometry, linkages, wheel-end assemblies, and drivetrain and brake mounting interfaces. Own mechanical design execution , developing concepts, detailed CAD models, engineering drawings, GD&T, and tolerance analyses to support prototype builds and production release. Sustain and improve existing platforms , investigating field issues, performing root cause analysis, and implementing validated engineering changes. Define chassis and vehicle dynamics requirements for ride quality, traction, braking, stability, ground clearance, and obstacle traversal across terrain and payload conditions. Provide technical oversight of supplier-developed hardware , reviewing designs, analyses, and test results to ensure systems meet vehicle requirements and integrate successfully. Develop and execute verification and validation plans with reliability, test, and integration teams, establishing measurable acceptance criteria for components and complete vehicles. Lead instrumented vehicle dynamics testing , analyze results, and translate findings into hardware improvements and operating limits. Partner with controls and autonomy engineers to characterize vehicle capabilities and improve motion performance. Support prototype builds, manufacturing, and service teams , resolving integration issues and improving durability, manufacturability, and maintainability . We’re excited about you because… You have a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related field. You have experience designing and developing suspension, chassis, or related mechanical systems for vehicles or mobile robots. You understand suspension kinematics, load transfer, tire behavior, stiffness and damping, braking, and vehicle stability—and can apply these fundamentals to hardware design. You are proficient in NX, SolidWorks, CATIA, or a comparable CAD platform and have experience releasing detailed mechanical designs. You apply sound engineering judgment to load cases, structural integrity, fatigue, bearings, bolted joints, materials, and manufacturing processes. You can independently assess designs and analyses, identify technical risks, and drive issues to resolution with internal teams and suppliers. You have hands-on experience with prototype assembly, instrumentation, vehicle testing, and root cause analysis. You can translate requirements into test methods and acceptance criteria, then use Python, MATLAB, or similar tools to evaluate results. You take ownership from initial investigation through implementation and verification Compensation The successful candidate’s starting pay will fall within the pay range listed below and is determined based on job-related factors including, but not limited to, skills, experience, qualifications, work location, and market conditions. Base salary is localized according to an employee’s work location. Ranges are market-dependent and may be modified in the future. In addition to base salary, the compensation for this role includes opportunities for equity grants. Talk to your recruiter for more information. DoorDash cares about you and your overall well-being. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package to all regular employees, which includes a 401(k) plan with employer matching, 16 weeks of paid parental leave, wellness benefits, commuter benefits match, paid time off and paid sick leave in compliance with applicable laws (e.g. Colorado Healthy Families and Workplaces Act). DoorDash also offers medical, dental, and vision benefits, 11 paid holidays, disability and basic life insurance, family-forming assistance, and a mental health program, among others. To learn more about our benefits, visit our careers page here . See below for paid time off details: For salaried roles: flexible paid time off/vacation, plus 80 hours of paid sick time per year. For hourly roles: vacation accrued at about 1 hour for every 25.97 hours worked (e.g. about 6.7 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 3.4 hours/month if working 20 hours/week), and paid sick time accrued at 1 hour for every 30 hours worked (e.g. about 5.8 hours/month if working 40 hours/week; about 2.9 hours/month if working 20 hours/week). The national base pay range for this position within the United States, including Illinois and Colorado. $109,500 — $161,000 USD About DoorDash At DoorDash, our mission to empower local economies shapes how our team members move quickly, learn, and reiterate in order to make impactful decisions that display empathy for our range of users—from Dashers to merchant partners to consumers. We are a technology and logistics company that started by enabling door-to-door delivery, and we are looking for team members who can help us go from a company that is known as the place you order food to a company that people turn to for any and all goods. DoorDash is growing rapidly and changing constantly, which gives our team members the opportunity to share their unique perspectives, solve new challenges, and own their careers. We're committed to supporting employees’ happiness, healthiness, and overall well-being by providing comprehensive benefits and perks including premium healthcare, wellness expense reimbursement, paid parental leave and more. jobs.description: POSITION SUMMARY: The role of a Laboratory Assistant I has the ability to receive specimens with an ability to exercise independent judgement in the performance of assigned laboratory tasks. This role ensures all workflow stations within the laboratory are given specimens in a timely manner, with turnaround time in consideration. cold_email.subject: Interest in Lab Assistant I — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Natera Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Lab Assistant I opportunity with Natera at Natera.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Process Development Associate Scientist
jobs.description: Career Category Scientific Job Description Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do. Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline and portfolio of medicines to treat heart disease, obesity and obesity-related conditions, rare diseases, inflammatory conditions and cancer. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Process Development Associate Scientist What we expect of you Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this vital role you will be responsible for developing cell culture and purification manufacturing processes for Amgen’s late-stage pipeline. cold_email.subject: Interest in Process Development Associate Scientist — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Process Development Associate Scientist opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: About the Team The New Verticals team is building the future of local commerce by expanding DoorDash beyond restaurants. We help customers get the groceries, convenience items, alcohol, retail, and other essentials they need, when they need them. The Consumer Growth team sits at the intersection of strategy, operations, product, and marketing. We identify the biggest opportunities to grow New Verticals, develop the strategies to pursue them, and bring them to life through customer-facing launches, campaigns, and product experiences. About the Role We’re looking for an Associate Manager to lead Consumer Growth GTM strategy for New Verticals. This person will shape how we bring priority merchants, categories, and customer behaviors to market, with a focus on bringing structure to a high volume of GTM opportunities and helping teams prioritize and execute them efficiently. You will own the business strategy behind major growth moments: defining the customer opportunity, sizing the potential, recommending where to invest, setting goals, and translating insights into clear GTM plans. You will work closely with Marketing, Product, Analytics, Finance, and Business Development to ensure our plans are both strategically sound and operationally executable. This is a highly visible role for someone who is equally comfortable digging into data, developing a point of view, and driving alignment across senior cross-functional stakeholders. You will manage a portfolio of initiatives with varying levels of complexity and make clear recommendations about where DoorDash should focus its limited resources for the greatest customer and business impact. Define the customer problem, business opportunity, target audience, value proposition, and path to impact. Set investment and customer strategy. Develop frameworks to prioritize GTM investments and determine the right level of support across initiatives. Create scalable playbooks for customer targeting, including audience strategy, targeting principles, and measurement approaches. Turn data into action. Build analyses and models using SQL and Excel to assess customer behavior, business performance, incrementality, and return on investment. Develop test-and-learn plans and translate results into clear recommendations for what we should do next. Lead cross-functional execution. Partner with Integrated Marketing, CRM, Paid Media, Creative, Product, Analytics, Finance, Partnerships, and Operations to bring strategies to market. Align teams on goals, audiences, measurement, timelines, risks, and decisions. Build the operating system for GTM. Bring rigor and structure to a high volume of growth opportunities. Create clear prioritization frameworks, repeatable playbooks, planning cadences, and decision mechanisms that help teams move faster and focus resources on the highest-impact initiatives. This role rewards operational rigor: ensuring the highest-impact activations are prioritized, well scoped, and efficiently executed. We’re excited about you because you have… 4+ years of experience in strategy, operations, consulting, growth, business operations, product strategy, investment banking, or a related analytical and cross-functional environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to build trust across teams, influence senior stakeholders, and navigate competing priorities with sound judgment. You know when to drive alignment, when to push back, and how to articulate a clear point of view while maintaining strong cross-functional relationships. Strong analytical skills, including comfort independently pulling data in SQL and building models in Excel. You use data to develop a point of view and make clear recommendations, not just report findings. Experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through execution and measurement. An operationally minded, low-ego approach. jobs.title: Fraud Operations Program Manager
jobs.location: Chicago, IL; Denver, CO; Lake Mary, FL; Westlake, TX
jobs.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Fraud Operations Program Manager will oversee high-impact projects that support business growth and strategic initiatives across Fraud Operations. This role serves as the primary point of contact between Fraud Ops and Product, as well as the Detection & Prevention team (among other teams), and is responsible for building Business Requirement Documents (BRDs) for new products, drafting memos, managing issues, and leading project work within Fraud Operations. A core focus of this role is ensuring smooth product rollouts and launches that impact Fraud Operations — driving readiness across people, process, and technology — while partnering with Fraud Ops leadership and frontline agents to continuously identify and act on improvement opportunities. This role is based in our Chicago, IL, Denver, CO, Westlake, TX, and Lake Mary, FL office(s), with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you'll do Act as the main liaison between Fraud Operations and Product, as well as the Detection & Prevention team (among other teams), ensuring Fraud Ops is represented and prepared throughout the product development lifecycle. Own launch readiness for new product rollouts and initiatives impacting Fraud Operations — coordinating readiness across people, process, and technology ahead of go-live. Develop and maintain Business Requirement Documents (BRDs) for new products and initiatives affecting Fraud Operations. Draft and circulate memos related to Fraud Ops implementations and updates, ensuring timely review and approval. Manage and resolve issues related to Fraud Operations as they are reported, driving root-cause resolution and timely closure. Partner closely with the Fraud Operations leadership team to plan for and de-risk upcoming launches, aligning staffing, training, and workflow changes with product timelines. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders — Product, Detection & Prevention, Engineering, and BPO vendor partners — to ensure effective communication and collaboration across all projects impacting Fraud Operations teams. Establish a cohesive vision for Fraud Operations-wide initiatives that span multiple teams, keeping efficiency and operational readiness at the forefront of decision-making. Work directly with frontline Fraud Ops agents to surface process gaps and improvement opportunities, translating field-level feedback into scoped initiatives. Provide guidance to the Fraud Operations team, fostering a culture of continuous improvement. What you bring Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent work experience. Excellent program/project management skills. 5+ years of experience in Fraud Operations, Trust & Safety, or a related risk/operations discipline. Strong understanding of fraud typologies and operational workflows across products (e.g., equities, crypto, event contracts). Experience managing multiple projects at once, involving stakeholders across business units. Strong written and verbal communication, analytical skills, project management ability, and strong attention to detail. Skilled at balancing multiple priorities, operating autonomously, and driving execution while favoring automation over manual processes. Builds and sustains strong, trust-based relationships across a wide range of cross-functional teams — Product, Engineering, Detection & Prevention, BPO vendor partners, and frontline Fraud Ops agents — with a high level of responsiveness given the breadth of stakeholders this role touches. Resourceful, persistent, and able to thrive in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. Base Pay Range: Zone 1 (Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY; Bellevue, WA; Washington, DC) $119,000 — $140,000 USD Zone 2 (Denver, CO; Westlake, TX; Chicago, IL) $105,000 — $123,000 USD Zone 3 (Lake Mary, FL; Clearwater, FL; Gainesville, FL) $93,000 — $109,000 USD Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Manager - Investigation — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Pfizer Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Manager - Investigation opportunity with Pfizer at Pfizer.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. This role combines compute architecture, high-speed digital design, onboard power electronics, and compact HDI PCB development. We’re looking for a self-driven engineer who takes ownership from concept through deployment. Above all, you should enjoy hands-on engineering: bringing up boards, characterizing interfaces, and tracking challenging failures to their root cause. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Own compute hardware architecture and development, from component selection and schematic design through PCB layout, validation, and deployment. - Design and integrate high-speed interfaces—including PCIe, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, USB, and DisplayPort—balancing bandwidth, connectivity, power, and signal integrity. - Develop onboard DC-to-DC conversion and power distribution to meet efficiency, transient-response, sequencing, and power-integrity requirements. - Define HDI PCB stackups, dielectric materials, via structures, and routing strategies that balance electrical performance, manufacturability, reliability, and cost. - Lead bench bring-up and validation, including test planning, high-speed interface characterization, power measurements, and debugging through verified resolution. - Partner with thermal, mechanical, EMC, and software teams to integrate compute hardware into tightly constrained robotic systems. Own the metrics behind it: inbound case volume by driver, drivers fixed at the root, and time from first case to shipped fix, alongside the response-time and CSAT targets Product Support Operations already runs on. Own the customer's experience of getting unblocked: how quickly a user reaches a resolution and how little friction they hit on the way, whether Claude resolves the case or hands it to a specialist. Minimize the blast radius of novel issues. New models and product changes will keep creating new drivers no one can predict; catch each one at its first reports, assess impact, and get the fix prioritized while the affected group is still small. Partner with engineering and data science to build the systems that scale with Anthropic’s growth: Claude as the first responder, the data pipeline behind driver detection, and the tooling that lets Claude hand a diagnosed case to the right team. Own the trade-off framework between intake reduction, response time, cost, and quality, making transparent prioritization decisions about which drivers get fixed first and communicating them clearly to Product Support and senior leadership. Scaled through hypergrowth in support-heavy environments (consumer subscriptions, developer platforms, or fintech). Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Software Engineer opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role Robinhood set out to open the financial system to the many, not the few. We've done it for tens of millions of people in the US—now we're expanding into Canada. This is one of the most ambitious expansion initiatives for the company, and you'd be sitting at the center of it. We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. As a Product Manager on the Canada Expansion team, you'll manage localized product offerings, own end-to-end product experiences tailored for Canadian users, and work with experts in data, design, engineering, marketing, operations, and regulatory affairs to bring ideas to life that will help us democratize finance in Canada. This role is based in our Toronto office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do The International PM team's goal is simple to say and hard to do: democratize finance globally. That means scaling our products to work across many regions and building market-specific experiences that serve customers where they are. As a Staff PM on this team, you'll own product strategy and execution in Canada and set the playbook for user acquisition, growth, and localized offerings across the country. Additionally, you will: - Ship tailored financial products into the Canadian market working shoulder-to-shoulder with cross-functional teams. Bring together product development teams to craft and communicate a Canada-focused product vision and set of priorities that address the specific financial needs of Canadian consumers. Drive the roadmap—adapting existing trading features and building local tax-advantaged features and funding rails. Develop strong, collaborative relationships across design, engineering, and operations at the team and organizational levels. Partner with leaders in communications, compliance, content, customer experience, and marketing to ensure our vision, products, and progress are well understood. Ensure parity of product lines across US & global markets What you bring 6+ years as PM of direct product management experience building high-quality consumer products and growth efforts Ideally past experience working on a global consumer facing product Demonstrated history of using research, experimentation and analytics to guide decision making Experience working with and coordinating across globally dispersed teams Past experience working with engineering, design, research, legal, compliance and marketing in previous roles Excellent communication and collaboration skills Passion for financial products that improve people’s financial lives. Motivation to be a self-starter. Open to travel Willingness to work in EST English proficiency is required What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, and equity ownership Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including supplemental health insurance, ancillary insurance, and mental health support programs Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible employer-paid benefits spending account expenses beyond traditional benefits such as wellness, childcare, learning, and more. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, paid volunteer time off, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. Monthly commuter stipend to help offset in-office commuting costs Our team is committed to providing an inclusive and welcoming interview experience for all candidates. If you require a specific accommodation during the application or interview process due to a physical or mental condition, please complete this Applicant Accommodation Form to notify our team. The form should only be completed if you need a specific accommodation. Vacancy Notice: This job posting represents an existing vacancy that we are actively seeking to fill. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed. Base Pay Range: Toronto, ON $191,250 — $225,000 CAD Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.
